title.en: Minister condemns riot but urges review of police anti-racism guidance following Henry Nowak death – UK politics live
title.zh: 亨利·诺瓦克去世后，部长谴责骚乱，但敦促审查警方反种族主义指导 – 英国政治直播

summary.en: Sarah Jones appeals for calm after rioting over the death of Nowak, who was handcuffed while dying from stab wound Yesterday Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, delivered what he called an “emergency address to the nation” on YouTube at around this time. In it, he claimed that...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Sarah Jones appeals for calm after rioting over the death of Nowak, who was handcuffed while dying from stab wound Yesterday Nigel Farage, the Reform UK leader, delivered what he called an “emergency address to the nation” on YouTube at around this time. In it, he claimed that the Henry Nowak case was proof that white people were treated unfairly in the UK. He said that George Floyd (whom he described as a “career criminal”) died in policy custody in the US, there was a surge in support for the Black Lives Matter campaign, with Keir Starmer taking the knee. But nothing remotely similar has occurred after the death of Nowak, Farage claimed. Silence, absolute silence, proof, if ever there was any, that we’re living in a two-tier culture in this country where the rights and privileges of white people matter less than those of ethnic minorities. Enough of anti white prejudice a promotion of the idea that white lives matter just as much as black lives. An end to DEI [diversity, equity and inclusion] and positive discrimination, but a country that treats everybody equally and fairly before the law. This is serious. This is urgent. I fear for where our society would be in a few short years if we don’t grip this and do it very, very quickly. I don’t think the evidence at the moment would suggest that, if you look at the facts and figures about policing. I will always listen to the police in terms of what they’re saying and the home secretary said yesterday [that] we need to talk to the police. We need to talk to the Sikh community. We need to talk to knife crime campaigners. We need to understand what it is we need to do differently and better and we will do that. Continue reading...
body.zh: 诺瓦克因刺伤死亡时被戴上手铐，引发骚乱，莎拉·琼斯呼吁民众保持冷静昨天，改革英国领导人奈杰尔·法拉奇大约在这个时候在 YouTube 上发表了他所谓的“向全国发出的紧急讲话”。他在其中声称亨利·诺瓦克案证明白人在英国受到不公平对待。他说，乔治·弗洛伊德（他将其描述为“职业罪犯”）在美国政策拘留期间死亡，对“黑人生命也是命”运动的支持激增，凯尔·斯塔默下跪。但法拉奇声称，诺瓦克去世后没有发生任何类似的事情。沉默，绝对的沉默，证明，如果有的话，证明我们生活在这个国家的两层文化中，白人的权利和特权比少数民族的权利和特权更重要。反白人偏见已经够多了，我们应该提倡白人的生命与黑人的生命同样重要的观念。 DEI（多元化、公平和包容）和积极歧视的终结，而是一个在法律面前平等和公平对待每个人的国家。这很严重。这很紧急。我担心，如果我们不抓住这一点并非常非常快地采取行动，我们的社会在短短几年内会变成什么样子。如果你看看有关警务的事实和数据，我认为目前的证据并不表明这一点。我将始终听取警方的意见，内政大臣昨天表示我们需要与警方交谈。我们需要与锡克教社区交谈。我们需要与刀具犯罪活动人士交谈。我们需要了解我们需要以不同的方式做得更好，我们会这样做。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to justice, dignity, and accountability. Micah 6:8 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with justice tempered by mercy, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到公义、尊严与问责。Micah 6:8提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以带着怜悯的公义来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: US plans extra tariffs for 60 countries over forced labor
title.zh: 美国计划对60个国家加征关税，理由是强迫劳动

summary.en: The US government is planning to impose additional tariffs on goods from 60 countries, citing concerns over forced labor practices. This move could disrupt existing trade agreements and ongoing negotiations with various US trade partners.
summary.zh: 美国政府计划对来自60个国家的商品加征额外关税，理由是担忧这些国家存在强迫劳动行为。此举可能会扰乱美国与多个贸易伙伴已签署的贸易协议及正在进行的谈判。

body.en:
A new wave of Trump tariffs could unsettle US trade partners which have already signed new trade deals or have been negotiating them for months.

US President Donald Trump's administration is proposing additional tariffs of 10% or more to be imposed on its trading partners following a probe into countries importing goods allegedly made with forced labor.

In a report released Wednesday, the US Trade Representative (USTR) said it had found that 60 economies had failed to "impose and effectively enforce a prohibition on the importation of goods produced with forced labor," calling it a "burden" to US commerce.

"This creates a dynamic where American workers are forced to compete globally on an unlevel playing field. We will no longer tolerate this disparity," USTR Ambassador Jamieson Greer said in the document.

The tariff proposal is currently open to public comment and review and is therefore not in immediate effect.

The new tariffs under US trade law could help Trump bypass the Supreme Court ruling in February which stated that his tariffs were largely illegal.

An additional 10% tariff will be imposed on imports from Canada, Mexico, Taiwan, Pakistan, the UK and EU nations. These are countries which, according to Washington's investigation, impose a forced labor import prohibition, that have undertaken commitments on forced labor or have partially prevented the import of forced labor goods.

An additional 12.5% tariff will be imposed on 45 others, including China, India, Japan, South Korea, Brazil and Switzerland. These are countries that have failed to impose and effectively enforce the prohibition of imports made with forced labor, the statement said.

"Each of our trading partners must do more to ensure that trade does not perversely encourage and entrench forced labor globally," Greer said.

The alleged failure to prohibit imports made with forced labor was "subjecting US producers to unfair competition" in both export markets and the US market, the USTR said.

The trade regulation body will hold hearings about the proposed tariffs on July 7.

This latest wave of tariffs is likely to unsettle several US trade partners , who have been negotiating lower levies for over a year.

Just two weeks ago, the EU approved a trade deal with Washington to cap tariffs on most EU exports at 15%. That consensus was hard fought , with some member nations initially threatening to block the deal.

Meanwhile, a US delegation is currently in New Delhi to finalize a trade deal after Washington imposed one of the highest tariffs on India last year. India's Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal on Monday told local media that key details of the deal were already settled.

The last set of tariffs, partially over India's import of Russian oil, had significantly soured...
body.zh: 特朗普的新一波关税可能会让已经签署新贸易协议或已经谈判数月的美国贸易伙伴感到不安。 在对进口据称使用强迫劳动制造的商品的国家进行调查后，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普政府提议对其贸易伙伴征收 10% 或以上的额外关税。 美国贸易代表 (USTR) 在周三发布的一份报告中表示，它发现 60 个经济体未能“实施并有效执行禁止进口强迫劳动生产的商品”，称其为美国商业的“负担”。 美国贸易代表办公室大使杰米森·格里尔在文件中表示：“这造成了一种动态，美国工人被迫在不公平的竞争环境中参与全球竞争。我们将不再容忍这种不平等。” 该关税提案目前正在接受公众评论和审查，因此不会立即生效。 美国贸易法规定的新关税可能有助于特朗普绕过最高法院二月份的裁决，该裁决称他的关税在很大程度上是非法的。 对来自加拿大、墨西哥、台湾、巴基斯坦、英国和欧盟国家的进口产品加征10%的关税。根据华盛顿的调查，这些国家实施了强迫劳动进口禁令、对强迫劳动做出了承诺或部分阻止了强迫劳动产品的进口。 将对中国、印度、日本、韩国、巴西和瑞士等45个国家额外征收12.5%的关税。声明称，这些国家未能实施并有效执行禁止进口强迫劳动产品的规定。 格里尔说：“我们每个贸易伙伴都必须采取更多措施，确保贸易不会在全球范围内反常地鼓励和巩固强迫劳动。” 美国贸易代表办公室表示，据称未能禁止进口强迫劳动产品，导致美国生产商在出口市场和美国市场都面临不公平竞争。 贸易监管机构将于 7 月 7 日就拟议关税举行听证会。 最新一波关税可能会让几个美国贸易伙伴感到不安，他们一年多以来一直在就降低关税进行谈判。 就在两周前，欧盟批准了与华盛顿的一项贸易协议，将大多数欧盟出口产品的关税限制在 15%。这一共识是经过艰苦努力才达成的，一些成员国最初威胁要阻止这项协议。 与此同时，在华盛顿去年对印度征收最高关税之一后，美国代表团目前正在新德里敲定一项贸易协议。印度商务部长皮尤什·戈亚尔周一对当地媒体表示，该交易的关键细节已经敲定。 上一轮关税，部分是针对印度进口俄罗斯石油，已显着恶化......

reflection.en: When policies are enacted to address human rights concerns like forced labor, they echo a biblical call to defend the vulnerable. Proverbs 31:8-9 reminds us to speak for those who cannot speak for themselves, advocating for the rights of the destitute. Such actions, though complex in their economic impact, highlight a moral imperative to protect the dignity...
reflection.zh: 当政策旨在解决强迫劳动等侵犯人权的问题时，这与圣经中捍卫弱者的呼召不谋而合。箴言31:8-9提醒我们要为那些不能为自己发声的人开口，为困苦人的权利辩护。此类行动，尽管其经济影响复杂，却凸显了保护所有人尊严的道德责任。

verse.textEn: Speak up for those who cannot speak for themselves, for the rights of all who are destitute. Speak up and judge fairly; defend the rights of the poor and needy.
verse.textZh: 你当为不能自辩的开口，为孤独的伸冤。你当开口按公义判断，为困苦和穷乏的辨屈。

title.en: Seven killed after drone hits bus in Russia-controlled part of Ukraine
title.zh: 无人机在俄罗斯控制的乌克兰地区撞上公共汽车，造成七人死亡

summary.en: The bus was travelling between Moscow and Simferopol, in Russian-occupied Crimea, an official says.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Seven people have been killed and 11 others injured after a drone hit a passenger bus travelling through a Russia-controlled part of Ukraine, an official said.

Denis Pushilin, the Kremlin-installed leader of Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region, said the bus was struck in the early hours of Wednesday as it was travelling between Moscow and Simferopol, in Russian-occupied Crimea.

Black smoke could also be seen rising over St Petersburg on Wednesday morning, with Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelensky confirming the city's oil terminal had been hit.

The attack comes as the city hosts the annual International Economic Forum, an event designed to showcase Russia to the world.

The strikes come a day after a massive Russian assault on cities across Ukraine killed at least 22 people, including several women and children.

On the drone which hit the bus in Donetsk, Pushilin said: "In Yenakiyevo, a UAV attacked a Moscow-Simferopol coach; according to preliminary reports, seven civilians were killed."

Drones were downed over Belgorod, Kursk and other western regions, as well as near Moscow and over the Sea of Azov, Russian officials added.

At least 50 of the drones were downed over the Leningrad region northwest of Moscow, according to the regional governor Alexander Drozdenko.

The region includes St Petersburg, which is welcoming delegates from around the world for the economic forum from Wednesday.

"Important facilities on Russian territory were hit last night," Zelensky wrote on X, sharing a video of black smoke rising above St Petersburg.

He described the strikes as "long-range sanctions" and said Ukrainian forces also hit military targets in Russia's Tambov region.

These overnight strikes saw Pulkovo airport temporarily restrict flights, according to Russian aviation watchdog Rosaviatsia.

Meanwhile, an 86-year-old woman was killed following a drone attack in Ukraine's southern Kherson region overnight, Yaroslav Shanko, head of the city's military administration said.

This came as part of a wider attack by Moscow overnight, with Ukraine's air force saying Russia launched 198 drones at several different regions, 189 of which were shot down.

The latest wave of strikes comes a day after Russia launched one of its largest attacks on Ukraine since its full-scale invasion began in 2022.

At least 22 people were killed after Russia launched more than 700 missiles and drones overnight into Tuesday, Ukrainian officials said.

Russia's defence ministry said the strikes had been a response to previous Ukrainian attacks, saying in a statement that the "strike objectives" had all been achieved.

The Kremlin said on Tuesday it was carrying out the "systematic strikes" it had pledged after accusing Kyiv of a deadly attack on a student dormitory in an occupied...
body.zh: 一名官员称，一架无人机撞上一辆途经俄罗斯控制的乌克兰地区的客车，造成 7 人死亡、11 人受伤。 克里姆林宫任命的乌克兰东部顿涅茨克地区领导人丹尼斯·普希林表示，这辆巴士于周三凌晨在莫斯科和俄罗斯占领的克里米亚辛菲罗波尔之间行驶时被撞。 周三早上，圣彼得堡上空也可见黑烟升起，乌克兰总统泽伦斯基证实该市的石油码头遭到袭击。 此次袭击发生之际，该市正在举办一年一度的国际经济论坛，该论坛旨在向世界展示俄罗斯。 一天前，俄罗斯对乌克兰各城市发动大规模袭击，造成至少 22 人死亡，其中包括几名妇女和儿童。 关于在顿涅茨克袭击公共汽车的无人机，普希林说：“在叶纳基耶沃，一架无人机袭击了莫斯科-辛菲罗波尔的一辆长途汽车；根据初步报告，有七名平民死亡。” 俄罗斯官员补充说，无人机在别尔哥罗德、库尔斯克和其他西部地区以及莫斯科附近和亚速海上空被击落。 莫斯科西北部列宁格勒地区州长亚历山大·德罗兹登科表示，至少有 50 架无人机在该地区被击落。 该地区包括圣彼得堡，从周三开始，圣彼得堡将欢迎来自世界各地的代表参加经济论坛。 “昨晚，俄罗斯境内的重要设施遭到袭击，”泽连斯基在 X 上写道，并分享了一段圣彼得堡上空升起黑烟的视频。 他将这次袭击描述为“远程制裁”，并表示乌克兰军队还袭击了俄罗斯坦波夫地区的军事目标。 据俄罗斯航空监管机构 Rosaviatsia 称，这些夜间罢工导致普尔科沃机场暂时限制航班。 与此同时，乌克兰南部赫尔松地区军事管理局局长雅罗斯拉夫·尚科(Yaroslav Shanko)表示，夜间，一名86岁的妇女在乌克兰南部赫尔松地区遭遇无人机袭击身亡。 这是莫斯科夜间更广泛袭击的一部分，乌克兰空军称俄罗斯向几个不同地区发射了 198 架无人机，其中 189 架被击落。 最新一波袭击发生前一天，俄罗斯对乌克兰发动了自 2022 年全面入侵乌克兰以来最大规模的袭击之一。 乌克兰官员称，俄罗斯在周二夜间发射了 700 多枚导弹和无人机，造成至少 22 人死亡。 俄罗斯国防部表示，此次袭击是对乌克兰此前袭击事件的回应，并在一份声明中表示，“打击目标”已全部实现。 克里姆林宫周二表示，在指责基辅对被占领的学生宿舍发动致命袭击后，正在实施其承诺的“系统性罢工”。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.

title.en: Rural UK ‘particularly at risk’ of diesel shortages if Iran war continues
title.zh: 若伊朗战争持续，英国乡村地区“尤其面临”柴油短缺风险

summary.en: An OECD forecast warns of significant economic risks from the ongoing conflict, predicting potential global recessions and shortfalls in key energy products if the Iran conflict extends to 2027. Rural areas in the UK are identified as particularly vulnerable to diesel shortages.
summary.zh: 经济合作与发展组织（OECD）预测，如果伊朗冲突持续到2027年，全球经济将面临衰退风险，关键能源产品可能出现短缺。报告指出，英国乡村地区尤其容易受到柴油短缺的影响。

body.en: OECD forecast sets out economic risks from conflict, pointing to potential shortfalls to key energy products OECD predicts spate of recessions globally if Iran conflict drags into 2027 Rural areas in the UK would be particularly at risk of diesel shortages if the conflict in Iran continues to squeeze supplies, the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development has warned. The OECD predicted economic growth of 0.9% in the UK this year – a modest upgrade from the 0.7% it feared in March when it last updated its forecasts. It said government spending will help to support the economy in the short term. Continue reading...
body.zh: 经合组织的预测列出了冲突带来的经济风险，指出关键能源产品可能出现短缺。经合组织预测，如果伊朗冲突持续到 2027 年，全球将出现一系列衰退。经济合作与发展组织警告称，如果伊朗冲突继续挤压供应，英国农村地区将尤其面临柴油短缺的风险。经合组织预计英国今年的经济增长为 0.9%，较 3 月份上次更新预测时担心的 0.7% 略有上调。报告称，政府支出将有助于短期内支撑经济。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The prospect of prolonged conflict reminds us how deeply global events can impact daily life, even far from the front lines, threatening essential resources. In times when economic stability feels uncertain and scarcity looms, Habakkuk's ancient words offer a profound perspective: even if material provisions fail, we can still find joy and strength in 雅伟.
reflection.zh: 长期冲突的前景提醒我们，全球事件如何深刻影响日常生活，即使远离前线，也可能威胁到基本资源。在经济稳定感到不确定、短缺迫近的时期，哈巴谷的古老话语提供了一个深刻的视角：即使物质供应匮乏，我们仍能在雅伟中找到喜乐和力量。

verse.textEn: Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines... yet I will rejoice in Yahweh.
verse.textZh: 虽然无花果树不发旺，葡萄树不结果……然而，我要因雅伟欢欣。

title.en: Democracy in Africa: Coups, crises and foregone conclusions
title.zh: 非洲民主：政变、危机与既定结局

summary.en: As Ethiopia formally counts the votes following Monday's election, attitudes toward democracy appear to be shifting across Africa. In April, Burkina Faso's junta leader told the Burkinabe people to "forget" democracy.
summary.zh: 埃塞俄比亚在周一选举后正式计票之际，非洲各地对民主的态度似乎正在转变。四月，布基纳法索的军政府领导人告诉布基纳法索人民“忘记”民主。

body.en:
As Ethiopia formally counts the votes following Monday's election, attitudes toward democracy appear to be shifting across Africa. In April, Burkina Faso's junta leader told the Burkinabe people to "forget" democracy.

Many of  the 2026 elections across Africa  across Africa are marked by fraud, repression and a growing disconnect between young people and political elites.  

Though results have yet to be announced, Monday's election in Ethiopia , for example, is widely expected to result in a win for incumbent Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, despite deep divisions in the nation. Officials cited security concerns in suspending voting in parts of the country; the entire Tigray region was excluded from the election as tensions continue between regional and federal authorities. Tigray has not had federal representation for six years, and regional fighters fought a bloody civil war with federal forces from 2020 to 2022. 

In West Africa, Ibrahim Traore, who seized power in the 2022 coup in  Burkina Faso , told the Burkinabe people in April to "forget" about democracy .

"If an African wants to tell you about democracy, you should run away," he said on the state broadcaster, RTB. "Democracy kills."

Traore's statement shocked many, yet it also resonated with parts of the population. In Burkina Faso's capital, Ouagadougou, some residents argued that there is no time for democracy, as the fights  against terror groups and for economic rebuilding take priority.

The national militaries over threw the governments of Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger and Guinea from 2020 through 2023. In Guinea-Bissau, a coup  took place in 2025 .

Now led by military juntas, Niger, Mali and Burkina Faso formally withdrew from the regional ECOWAS   bloc in January 2025 and established their own partnership , the Alliance of Sahel States (AES).

The trend extends beyond West Africa. Further south in Gabon, the military took power in 2023, while in the Central African nation of Chad, a transitional military council governed until 2025.

In Chad, in Central Africa, Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno succeeded his father, Idriss Deby Itno, as president after the elder was killed by rebels in 2021, ending his 30-year rule.

In Sudan , in North Africa, a struggle between rival factions escalated into a full-scale civil war .

A 2023 report from the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) cites "multidimensional poverty, inequality, manipulation of constitutional term limits, limited youth and women's participation, governance deficits and higher levels of military expenditure" as factors that increase the risk of coups.

body.zh: 随着埃塞俄比亚在周一选举后正式计票，整个非洲对民主的态度似乎正在发生转变。四月，布基纳法索军政府领导人告诉布基纳法索人民“忘记”民主。 非洲各地 2026 年的许多选举都存在欺诈、镇压以及年轻人与政治精英之间日益脱节的现象。 例如，尽管结果尚未公布，但人们普遍预计周一在埃塞俄比亚举行的选举将导致现任总理阿比·艾哈迈德获胜，尽管该国国内存在深刻分歧。官员们出于安全考虑暂停了该国部分地区的投票；由于地区和联邦当局之间的紧张关系持续存在，整个提格雷地区被排除在选举之外。提格雷已经六年没有联邦代表权，2020年至2022年期间，地区武装分子与联邦军队进行了血腥的内战。 在西非，在 2022 年布基纳法索政变中夺取政权的易卜拉欣·特拉奥雷 (Ibrahim Traore) 在 4 月份告诉布基纳法索人民“忘记”民主。 “如果一个非洲人想告诉你民主，你就应该逃跑，”他在国家广播公司 RTB 上说道。 “民主会杀人。” 特劳雷的言论震惊了许多人，但也引起了部分民众的共鸣。在布基纳法索首都瓦加杜古，一些居民认为没有时间实行民主，因为打击恐怖组织和经济重建是当务之急。 2020 年至 2023 年期间，国家军队推翻了马里、布基纳法索、尼日尔和几内亚政府。几内亚比绍于 2025 年发生了政变。 现在，在军政府的领导下，尼日尔、马里和布基纳法索于 2025 年 1 月正式退出西非经共体区域集团，并建立了自己的伙伴关系——萨赫勒国家联盟 (AES)。 这一趋势已延伸到西非以外的地区。再往南，在加蓬，军方于 2023 年掌权，而在中非国家乍得，过渡军事委员会的执政期至 2025 年。 在中非乍得，穆罕默德·伊德里斯·代比·伊特诺 (Mahamat Idriss Deby Itno) 于 2021 年被叛乱分子杀害，继父伊德里斯·代比·伊特诺 (Idriss Deby Itno) 继任总统，结束了他 30 年的统治。 在北非的苏丹，敌对派别之间的斗争升级为全面内战。 联合国开发计划署 (UNDP) 2023 年的一份报告将“多维贫困、不平等、操纵宪法任期限制、青年和妇女参与有限、治理赤字和更高水平的军事支出”列为增加政变风险的因素。 该研究还发现，“当公民对民选政府的交付感到失望时，他们......

reflection.en: The shifting attitudes towards democracy in Africa highlight the profound impact of leadership on a nation's people. When leaders prioritize their own power over the well-being of their citizens, societies often experience distress. This reminds us that true governance should aim for the flourishing of all, fostering an environment where people can thrive...
reflection.zh: 非洲对民主态度的转变，凸显了领导力对一个国家人民的深远影响。当领导人将自身权力置于公民福祉之上时，社会往往会经历困境。这提醒我们，真正的治理应以所有人的繁荣为目标，营造一个人民能够兴盛而非在压迫下呻吟的环境。

title.en: US and Iran launch new strikes, as Kuwait says airport hit by Iranian drones
title.zh: 美国军方称向一艘驶往伊朗的油轮发射了导弹

summary.en: US Central Command reported that a missile struck the engine room of an oil tanker after its crew failed to heed multiple warnings.
summary.zh: 美国中央司令部报告称，一艘油轮的船员在多次警告后仍未听从，其发动机舱被导弹击中。

body.en:
The US military said it launched "self-defence" strikes on Iran overnight, and shot down ballistic missiles and drones fired at ships and Gulf countries.

The strikes on Qeshm Island, in the Strait of Hormuz, were "in response to attempted attacks by Iran across the Middle East", US Central Command (Centcom) said.

Iran said it had attacked US bases and helicopters in a "regional country" using missiles and drones in retaliation. Centcom said Tehran fired two missiles at Kuwait and three at Bahrain, all of which broke apart or were intercepted.

Kuwait's army later said Iranian drones had hit its international airport, causing "significant" building damage and injuries to a number of people.

Air traffic was suspended on Wednesday morning. Ministry of defence spokesman Brigadier General Saud Abdulaziz Al-Otaibi described the attack as "criminal Iranian aggression". He said the wounded had received medical care.

The latest attacks come amid stalled ceasefire negotiations between the US and Iran, after talks on a deal to end the months-long war failed to advance over the weekend.

Centcom said the strike on Qeshm Island had targeted an Iranian military ground control station, and that the US military also shot down three attack drones that had been launched by Iran toward "civilian mariners that were rightfully transiting regional waters".

The IRGC said "disrupting the security of the Strait of Hormuz will carry a heavy price for the aggressive US military".

Centcom also said Iran had launched "several" ballistic missiles towards countries in the region. "Two Iranian missiles fired at Kuwait fell short or broke apart en route, and three missiles launched at Bahrain were immediately intercepted by US and Bahrain air defence forces."

Iran has repeatedly attacked targets in Bahrain and Kuwait, where US military bases are located.

Earlier, Centcom said it had struck and disabled an unladen oil tanker that was sailing towards Iran, as part of Washington's naval blockade on the Strait of Hormuz, which began on 13 April.

A US aircraft fired a Hellfire missile into the engine room of the Botswana-flagged M/T vessel, after its crew "ignored repeated warnings", it said.

Centcom also released footage purportedly showing the moment the tanker was hit on Tuesday.

The escalation comes after US President Donald Trump this week told his critics to "sit back and relax" , saying that Iran "really wants to make a deal, and it will be a good one for the USA".

US media earlier reported that Trump had requested edits to the terms of a potential peace deal, after meeting with senior aides to discuss extending the framework of a ceasefire.

body.zh: 美国表示，作为华盛顿对霍尔木兹海峡的海上封锁的一部分，它袭击了一艘驶向伊朗的空载油轮并使其“瘫痪”。 美国中央司令部（Centcom）在一份声明中表示，一架美国飞机向这艘悬挂博茨瓦纳国旗的 M/T 船的发动机舱发射了一枚地狱火导弹，此前该船的船员“无视反复警告”。 中央司令部还发布了一段视频，据称显示了周二油轮被击中的那一刻。伊朗尚未就此事发表公开评论。 4月13日，美国军方开始对所有进出伊朗港口的船只实施封锁。

reflection.en: This incident reminds us of the perilous path when warnings are unheeded and force is employed. The scripture cautions that those who resort to violence often face its consequences, highlighting the dangerous cycle that can easily escalate.
reflection.zh: 这一事件提醒我们，当警告被忽视并动用武力时，道路是多么危险。经文告诫我们，那些诉诸暴力的人常常会面临其后果，突显了容易升级的危险循环。

title.en: 'Australia has failed': US opens door to new tariffs in trade crackdown
title.zh: “澳大利亚失败了”：美国在贸易打击中向新关税敞开大门

summary.en: Donald Trump's administration has been scrambling to rebuild its tariff agenda after a US supreme court decision.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及管家责任、供应与公共福祉。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia is among 60 countries potentially facing new tariffs from the United States after the Trump administration accused them of failing to block goods made with "forced labour" — opening another front in the US' ongoing global trade war.

The US trade representative (USTR), Jamieson Greer, announced on Wednesday that his office had completed investigations into 60 economies and found their failure to act was "unreasonable" and harmful to US commerce.

"The failure of our most important trading partners to address the importation of goods made with forced labour is unacceptable," Greer said in a statement.

"This creates a dynamic where American workers are forced to compete globally on an unlevel playing field."

Proposed tariffs of up to 12.5 per cent on imports from the named countries, including Australia, will now go to a public comment period before any final decision is made.

The USTR has used a legal mechanism called Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 to investigate whether dozens of countries were doing enough to stop goods made with forced labour from entering their markets.

On Wednesday, it concluded that none of the 60 investigated countries passed the test.

That finding is important because it effectively gives the US a legal basis to impose new tariffs.

The proposed rates — 10 per cent for some countries at 12.5 per cent for others — will be subject to public submissions until 6 July, with a hearing scheduled for 7 July.

The announcement comes as the Trump administration scrambles to rebuild its tariff agenda after the US Supreme Court struck down Trump's tariffs in February.

Following that decision, the Trump administration imposed a global 10 per cent temporary tariff that is due to expire on 24 July.

Australia falls into the larger group of 54 countries the USTR says have no forced labour import ban whatsoever.

That puts it alongside China, Vietnam, Japan, the United Kingdom and New Zealand.

The findings document accuses Australia of having "failed to impose and effectively enforce a forced labour import prohibition", adding the acts, policies and practices of Australia are "unreasonable and burden or restrict US commerce".

That language is used almost identically across every other country on the list.

A spokesperson for Australia's Trade Minister Don Farrell pushed back on the characterisation.

"Australia has robust, comprehensive and world-leading legislation addressing forced labour and modern slavery," they said.

"We continue to use every opportunity to advocate that US tariffs imposed on Australia are unwarranted."

title.en: 'Paid for a Porsche, got a compact two-seater': Is this AUKUS' hidden cost?
title.zh: “花钱买保时捷，却得到一辆紧凑型双座车”：这是AUKUS的隐性成本吗？

summary.en: Experts state that the acquisition of used submarines does not alter Australia's AUKUS objectives, yet critics contend that the country is receiving an unfair deal.
summary.zh: 专家表示，购买二手潜艇不会改变澳大利亚的AUKUS目标，但批评人士认为，澳大利亚正在吃亏。

body.en:
The news that Australia will only receive "second-hand" Virginia-class submarines has become the latest fault line in the AUKUS debate, with critics questioning ballooning costs and questioning the value for money.

"You've paid for a Porsche, but they give you a compact two-seater," Albert Palazzo, adjunct professor at UNSW in Canberra and a former director of war studies for the Australian Army, told SBS News.

"If I was the consumer, I'd get angry. I paid for a Porsche, where's my Porsche?"

Under the agreement made in 2023 with the United States and United Kingdom , Australia would buy three Virginia-class nuclear-powered submarines from the US — one newly built, and two already 'in service'.

Last week, Defence Minister Richard Marles revealed that all three of the submarines would be in-service vessels from the US Navy. Marles said the new approach would be "cost-effective" and "streamline" the submarines' delivery.

Speaking to ABC radio on Wednesday, Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy said the arrangement was always the government's wish, and that it would be "simpler, cheaper to manage, and that's been confirmed by the Pentagon overnight as well".

A Virginia-class submarine is expected to have three refurbishments in its 33-year lifespan.

Jennifer Parker, a maritime security expert at the Australian National University Security College, said it's possible unforeseen costs could arise depending on the condition of the submarines.

It's unclear whether the US would refurbish the submarines before giving them to Australia, but Parker said it's reasonable to assume they would.

"If it is already of the age that it needs to have gone through its first one, which is about the 10-year mark, then you would expect that we would get [a refit]," she told SBS News.

Parker said it's a reassuring sign that Australia was receiving Virginia-class submarines, as opposed to the older Los Angeles-class submarines reaching the end of their life.

"I was a little bit surprised because I thought they might sell off the Los Angeles-class because they have less need for those," she said.

The 'in service' Virginia-class submarines Australia will receive are Block IV boats. They're 125m long and fitted with 12 missile launchers.

Later models of the Virginia-class submarine expanded their capability, with Block V growing to 140m in length and carrying 40 missiles.

Palazzo said the difference between the Block IV and Block VII would be "not trivial".

title.en: Shell pumped oil through Nigeria pipeline for years despite pollution evidence, documents show
title.zh: 文件显示，壳牌公司在有污染证据的情况下仍多年通过尼日利亚管道输送石油

summary.en: Documents reportedly show that Shell continued to operate an oil pipeline in Nigeria for years despite evidence of pollution. The oil company stated that these documents do not account for the complex operational context of the time.
summary.zh: 据报道，文件显示壳牌公司在有污染证据的情况下，仍多年通过尼日利亚的一条管道输送石油。该公司表示，这些文件没有考虑到当时复杂的运营环境。

body.en:
British multinational Shell continued operating a major oil pipeline in Nigeria for years even though it knew it was causing widespread pollution - despite a warning from its own staff and its own technical standards, internal documents obtained by the BBC show.

The files, including emails and presentations, reveal that a senior Shell executive cautioned as early as 2008 about the risks of continuing to pump millions of barrels of unrefined fuel through one of the company's main pipelines in Africa's biggest oil producer while it was subject to massive and destructive uncontrolled theft and infrastructure failures.

Across Nigeria's oil-rich southern Niger Delta, decades of oil spills have left a landscape deeply scarred, with wetlands increasingly coated in crude and contaminated sediment.

The BBC obtained the internal documents after Shell disclosed them as part of ongoing legal proceedings in the UK brought by communities living around the creeks and mangroves of the Niger Delta, who want Shell to be liable for the pollution caused by more than 100 leaks stemming from theft and illegal refining of oil between 2011 and 2013 that have damaged their health, environment and livelihoods.

The 60-mile (96.5km) Nembe Creek Trunk Line runs near the riverine community of Bille, which is made up of 45 islands, from inland oilfields to a coastal processing site for exporting.

The pipeline, which Shell sold last year, was one of its biggest, most expensive and ultimately most problematic bits of infrastructure in Nigeria. It was capable of carrying up to 150,000 barrels of oil a day, but was repeatedly hit by spills and targeted by illegal oil thieves.

In court papers the oil firm argues that most of the pollution has been caused by "large-scale oil theft, sabotage" and dozens of illegal refineries, and that its Nigerian subsidiary invested heavily over many years to reduce the risk of and response to spills.

In places like Bille, which the BBC visited last week, residents describe once-rich fishing grounds turning toxic and unusable.

"Before 2011, here was a beautiful area. People play here and go into the river," 64-year-old fisherman Balafama Augustus Bruce told the BBC.

A claimant in the case against Shell, Bruce said before all the spills, he was able to catch a variety of fish including sardines, catfish, tilapia and even oysters, but most are hard to find now or if caught, appear deformed.

"We used to fish around here. But because of the damage [the spills] have caused, nobody is fishing here again.

According to the UN, since 1958 when Shell sent its first shipment of oil from Nigeria, at least 13 million barrels - or 1.5 million tonnes - of crude oil have been spilled in at least 7,000 incidents.

body.zh: 英国跨国公司壳牌公司在尼日利亚运营一条主要石油管道多年，尽管它知道这会造成大范围的污染——尽管该公司自己的员工发出了警告，并遵循自己的技术标准，英国广播公司获得的内部文件显示。 这些文件（包括电子邮件和演示文稿）显示，壳牌的一位高级管理人员早在 2008 年就警告称，在该公司位于非洲最大石油生产国的一条主要管道遭受大规模破坏性失控盗窃和基础设施故障的情况下，继续通过该公司的一条主要管道输送数百万桶未精炼燃料的风险。 在尼日利亚石油资源丰富的尼日尔三角洲南部，数十年的石油泄漏事件给当地的土地留下了深深的伤痕，湿地越来越多地被原油和受污染的沉积物覆盖。 英国广播公司获得了这些内部文件，壳牌公司披露了这些内部文件，这是居住在尼日尔三角洲小溪和红树林周围社区在英国正在进行的法律诉讼的一部分，他们希望壳牌公司对 2011 年至 2013 年间因盗窃和非法炼油造成的 100 多起泄漏造成的污染承担责任，这些泄漏损害了他们的健康、环境和生计。 全长 60 英里（96.5 公里）的 Nembe Creek 干线靠近 Bille 河滨社区，该社区由 45 个岛屿组成，从内陆油田到沿海出口加工场。 壳牌去年出售的这条管道是其在​​尼日利亚最大、最昂贵、最终问题最多的基础设施之一。它每天能够运载多达15万桶石油，但屡屡发生漏油事件，并成为非法石油窃贼的目标。 该石油公司在法庭文件中辩称，大部分污染是由“大规模石油盗窃、破坏”和数十家非法炼油厂造成的，其尼日利亚子公司多年来投入巨资，以降低泄漏风险和应对措施。 在英国广播公司上周访问的比勒等地，居民们表示，曾经富饶的渔场现在变得有毒且无法使用。 “2011 年之前，这里是一个美丽的地区。人们在这里玩耍，进入河里，”64 岁的渔民巴拉法玛·奥古斯都·布鲁斯 (Balafama Augustus Bruce) 告诉 BBC。 作为针对壳牌案的索赔人，布鲁斯表示，在所有泄漏事件发生之前，他能够捕获各种鱼类，包括沙丁鱼、鲶鱼、罗非鱼，甚至牡蛎，但大多数现在很难找到，或者如果捕获，就会出现畸形。 “我们曾经在这附近钓鱼。但由于[泄漏]造成的损害，没有人再在这里钓鱼了。 据联合国称，自 1958 年壳牌从尼日利亚运送第一批石油以来，已发生至少 7,000 起事故，造成至少 1300 万桶（即 150 万吨）原油泄漏。 活动人士长期以来一直试图坚持...

title.en: Who is Bill Pulte, Trump's eyebrow-raising pick for US intelligence chief?
title.zh: 谁是比尔·普尔特，特朗普令人侧目的美国情报主管人选？

summary.en: Donald Trump's choice for acting US intelligence chief, Bill Pulte, has drawn criticism from both Democrats and some Republicans. Concerns have been raised regarding the appointment.

body.en:
Donald Trump has raised eyebrows and tempers amongst both Republicans and Democrats by appointing a man with zero experience as the United States' acting director of national intelligence. 

Bill Pulte, 38, is a staunch supporter of Trump and the grandson of William J Pulte, billionaire founder of the US housing construction firm PulteGroup.

He was appointed by the US president as the director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency in 2025, a position he will continue to hold as he takes on the intelligence role.

"William has deep experience managing the most sensitive matters in America, the safety and soundness of the Markets, and over 10 Trillion Dollars at Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac, a substantial increase from where it was just 12 months ago," Trump wrote in a social media post announcing the appointment.

"During this period, he will remain Director of the Federal Housing Finance Agency, and Chairman of Fannie Mae/Freddie Mac. Congratulations to Director Pulte!"

Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac are the names given to the Federal National Mortgage Association and the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation, government-sponsored enterprises that work to keep the US housing market affordable.

Pulte will take over the intelligence coordination role from Tulsi Gabbard, who has held the position since the start of Trump's second term. Gabbard clashed with Trump over Iran in March and later resigned from her role , citing family reasons.

The combative businessman nearly got into a physical altercation with US treasury secretary Scott Bessent during a private dinner for senior officials. According to US media, Bessent threatened to punch Pulte "in the fu—ing face" for allegedly criticising him to Trump.

As housing director, he appointed himself the head of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac, firing senior executives who opposed his unilateral decision-making.

He is credited with devising the 50-year mortgage plans that have been touted by Trump, and with giving Trump the idea to share a controversial meme of himself as Jesus Christ, according to US reports.

Pulte also used his access to mortgage records to refer some of Trump's top political opponents for prosecution, earning him the nickname "Little Trump".

New York attorney-general Letitia James, a Democrat who had previously opposed the US president, was charged with mortgage fraud in a case that was later dropped.

title.en: 'Some kind of apocalypse': 40,000 people shelter in Kyiv metro amid major Russian attack
title.zh: “某种末日景象”：俄罗斯大规模袭击下，4万人涌入基辅地铁避难

summary.en: Russian attacks killed at least 22 people across Ukraine overnight. Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned more attacks could follow.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯一夜之间在乌克兰各地发动袭击，造成至少22人死亡。弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基警告称，可能还会有更多袭击。

body.en:
More than 40,000 people took shelter in Kyiv's metro system overnight as Russia launched one of its largest attacks of its war on Ukraine , killing at least 22 people and wounding 130 across the country.

The strike, which Ukrainian officials said involved 73 missiles and 656 drones, was the third heavy assault on the capital in under a month.

Russia ‌has targeted Ukraine's power supply and infrastructure in a war more than four years old, while Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Russian oil facilities.

The Kremlin warned that it ‌intended "systematic strikes" on targets in Kyiv in response to a drone attack on a dormitory in Ukraine's Russian-held region of Luhansk, which killed 21.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Authorities said 16 people — including two children — died in the south-eastern city of Dnipro when a four-storey apartment building collapsed. Seven were killed in Kyiv.

Anastasia, a Kyiv resident whose building was damaged in the attack, described a "loud" and "terrifying" night huddled in her bathroom before evacuating.

"All the windows were blown out completely; there are no windows at all. It wasn't just one explosion here all night," she told Agence France-Presse. "The night here was just a nightmare."

Another resident, Olha Mudra, spoke to Reuters at the site of one strike with her six-year-old daughter Natalia, her face and clothes covered in dust.

"We couldn't understand what was happening," she told Reuters. "Some kind of apocalypse?"

Kyiv's metro — 46 stations across the city — has become an emergency refuge for the capital under bombardment.

Kyiv Metro said more than 41,000 people, including almost 4,500 children, sheltered in its subway network during the shelling.

"This is the highest number of people in the metro during a nighttime air raid in recent years," Kyiv Metro said. "During an air raid alert, 46 underground metro stations operate in shelter-in-place mode, and all lobbies are open for entry without exception.

"There are usually fewer people at central stations during an air raid alert. Therefore, the metro recommends using them in times of danger, if possible."

Kyiv Metro advised people seeking shelter not to bring bulky items or tents so that more people could use the space, and asked passengers to be considerate of staff working through the night to keep the network running.

It also advised those sheltering to bring warm clothes, blankets and sleeping mats, noting the underground temperature sits at 17 to 18 degrees.

title.en: Mysteriously missing congressman wins primary after Trump endorsement
title.zh: 神秘失踪的国会议员在特朗普背书后赢得初选

summary.en: Republican lawmaker Tom Kean Jr. won his primary election despite having been absent from both Washington D.C. and his New Jersey district for several months, with no public explanation for his disappearance.
summary.zh: 共和党议员小汤姆·基恩在缺席华盛顿及其新泽西州选区数月后，仍赢得了初选，其失踪原因至今未公开。

body.en:
Republican Congressman Tom Kean Jr, who has not been seen in Washington or his New Jersey district for months, secured his party's nomination for re-election on Tuesday, after receiving a recent endorsement from President Donald Trump.

"Tom Kean has my Complete and Total Endorsement for Re-Election," Trump wrote on social media, adding, "HE WILL NEVER LET YOU DOWN!"

Kean ran unopposed in the Republican primary and did not need to campaign for votes. But US media report he also has been absent from Congress, missing more than 100 votes.

In November's midterm elections, Kean will face Democrat Rebecca Bennett, a former US Navy helicopter pilot, who won her party's primary on Tuesday.

Kean was last seen on 5 March. His staff said in April that he was dealing with a medical issue. But Kean's continued absence has become a national curiosity in the US.

In his endorsement posted to Truth Social on Monday, Trump wrote that Kean was a "Tremendous Advocate of our America First Agenda" and "is working tirelessly".

Shortly after his last vote in Congress in March, colleagues, Republican officials and news organisations reported concerns about his whereabouts. Text messages went unanswered, as did requests for interviews.

In the statement released by his office on 27 April, he said he expected to be back soon.

"My doctors continue to assure me that my recovery will be complete and that I will be back to the job I love very soon," Kean said in the statement, posted on X.

Nearly a month later, Kean participated in a telephone interview with the New Jersey Globe and reiterated his intent to run for re-election and return to public life.

"I understand the need for public transparency, and I appreciate the support of my constituents," he said.

"I anticipate that in the next couple of weeks, I'll return to voting and to the campaign trail."

As voters began casting ballots in the election on Tuesday, there still had been no reported sightings of Kean.

The district he represents is considered a swing district, meaning it has a high propensity to flip between Republicans and Democrats each election cycle.

His will be a key district for Republicans to hold on to in November's midterm elections, which will determine the balance of power in Congress. Democrats are looking to unseat him and shift power their way and deliver Trump a loss.

Trump's endorsement of Kean given the stakes is unsurprising. The US president also has not shied away from endorsing candidates, even as they court controversy - or mystery.
body.zh: 共和党众议员小汤姆·基恩已经几个月没有出现在华盛顿或新泽西选区，在最近得到唐纳德·特朗普总统的支持后，他于周二获得了共和党的连任提名。 特朗普在社交媒体上写道：“我完全支持汤姆·基恩连任，他永远不会让你失望！” 基恩在共和党初选中没有遭到反对，也不需要竞选选票。但美国媒体报道称，他也缺席国会，缺席了 100 多张选票。 在 11 月的中期选举中，基恩将面对民主党人丽贝卡·贝内特 (Rebecca Bennett)，她是前美国海军直升机飞行员，于周二赢得了党内初选。 基恩最后一次出现是在 3 月 5 日。他的工作人员四月份表示，他正在处理健康问题。但基恩的持续缺席已经成为美国全国的好奇心。 特朗普在周一发表在《Truth Social》上的背书中写道，基恩是“我们美国第一议程的杰出倡导者”，并且“正在不知疲倦地工作”。 三月份他在国会最后一次投票后不久，同事、共和党官员和新闻机构都报告了对他行踪的担忧。短信和采访请求都没有得到回复。 在他的办公室4月27日发布的声明中，他表示他预计很快就会回来。 基恩在 X 上发布的声明中表示：“我的医生继续向我保证，我将会完全康复，并且我很快就会回到我喜欢的工作岗位。” 近一个月后，基恩接受了《新泽西环球报》的电话采访，重申了竞选连任并重返公共生活的意图。 “我理解公共透明度的必要性，我感谢选民的支持，”他说。 “我预计在接下来的几周内，我将重返投票和竞选活动。” 当选民周二开始为选举投票时，仍然没有看到基恩的报道。 他所代表的选区被认为是摇摆选区，这意味着每个选举周期都有很高的在共和党和民主党之间翻转的倾向。 他的选区将成为共和党在11月中期选举中守住的关键选区，这将决定国会的权力平衡。民主党人正寻求推翻他并转移权力，让特朗普遭受损失。 考虑到风险，特朗普对基恩的支持并不令人意外。美国总统也不回避支持候选人，即使他们引起争议或神秘。

title.en: El Nino could push temperatures higher, UN warns
title.zh: 联合国警告厄尔尼诺现象可能推高气温

summary.en: The World Meteorological Organization has issued a warning about a high likelihood of a moderate to strong El Nino weather phenomenon in the coming months, which is expected to increase global temperatures and affect rainfall patterns.
summary.zh: 世界气象组织警告称，未来几个月出现中度或强度厄尔尼诺现象的可能性很高，这可能导致气温升高并影响降雨。

body.zh: 世界气象组织表示，未来几个月很可能出现中度或强烈的厄尔尼诺天气现象。这可能会导致气温升高并影响降雨。 联合国气象机构周二发布最新消息，预测今年 6 月至 8 月期间发生厄尔尼诺事件的可能性为 80%。 据世界气象组织称，厄尔尼诺现象是太平洋中部和东部海水温度周期性升高的现象，通常持续 9 至 12 个月。 这种天气模式可能导致全球气温升高，增加世界某些地区的降雨量，并引发其他地区的干旱，同时还会刺激中太平洋和东太平洋的飓风形成。 世界气象组织表示，厄尔尼诺现象在 6 月至 8 月期间发生的可能性为 80%，如果厄尔尼诺现象开始的话，其持续到至少 11 月的可能性“接近或高于 90%”。 世界气象组织表示：“尽管厄尔尼诺现象峰值强度和时间仍存在一些不确定性，但大多数预测模型表明，厄尔尼诺现象至少会是温和的，而且可能会很强。” 世界气象组织最高官员表示，为最严重的情况做好准备是谨慎的做法。 世界气象组织秘书长塞莱斯特·索洛表示：“我们需要为可能出现的强烈厄尔尼诺事件做好准备，这将加剧干旱和强降雨，并增加陆地和海洋发生热浪的风险。” 其他相关风险可能包括蚊子或蜱虫等昆虫传播的疾病患病率上升，以及食物和水供应减少。 可可等易受气候变化影响的高危作物也可能面临异常歉收。 几个月来，世界气象组织和其他组织一直在收集并注意到可能出现厄尔尼诺现象的迹象，这在很大程度上是由于海洋温度较高。 2023 年至 2024 年期间的最后一次厄尔尼诺现象导致 2024 年成为全球有记录以来最热的一年。 联合国秘书长安东尼奥·古特雷斯在视频声明中表示：“厄尔尼诺现象将为全球变暖火上浇油。” “影响将更加严重、传播得更远，并以毁灭性的速度跨越国界。” 他表示，“唯一有效的应对措施是应对危机的气候行动”，例如结束对化石燃料的“成瘾”，加速向可再生能源的转变，保护最弱势群体，并为所有人提供早期预警系统，这似乎是长期计划和未来几个月更直接的缓解方法之间的混合和匹配。 该警告是在初夏热浪给西欧一些地区带来创纪录的五月气温后不久发出的。 它还恰逢印度等亚洲部分地区的典型高温......

title.en: Kosovo general election: the cost of political polarization
title.zh: 科索沃大选：政治两极分化的代价

summary.en: Sunday's election in Kosovo, the third in under 16 months, highlights the deep political polarization marked by a clash between former allies, Prime Minister Albin Kurti and ex-President Vjosa Osmani. This internal division has led to a deadlock in dialogue with Serbia and created obstacles to Kosovo's integration...
summary.zh: 科索沃周日的选举是近16个月来的第三次，凸显了严重的政治两极分化，其特点是前盟友总理阿尔宾·库尔蒂和前总统维约萨·奥斯马尼之间的冲突。这种内部纷争导致与塞尔维亚的对话陷入僵局，并为科索沃融入欧盟制造了障碍。

body.en:
Sunday's election in Kosovo — the third in under 16 months — is marked by a clash between former allies PM Albin Kurti and ex-President Vjosa Osmani, deadlock in the dialogue with Serbia and obstacles to EU integration.

The current election campaign in Kosovo is marked not only by the usual competition between rival political parties, but also by the disintegration of one of the most important political alliances in the country in recent years, namely that of Prime Minister Albin Kurti , who has led the government for the past six years, and former President Vjosa Osmani .

Osmani was already a political ally of Albin Kurti and had the prime minister's support when she was elected president by the parliament of Kosovo in 2021.

At the time, the two were seen as a motor for change and the fight against corruption in Kosovo. Now, they are rivals.

When Osmani's term came to an end earlier this year, Kurti did not back her for a second term.

Kurti has said that "the president should be a unifying and representative figure," and that, in his view, Osmani has political ambitions to become involved in a political party and seek direct support from voters.

Instead, the prime minister put forward candidates from his own party, Vetevendosje. But opposition lawmakers did not rally behind these candidates .

Sunday's snap general election — Kosovo's third in just under 16 months — was triggered when Kosovo's parliament in April failed for the second time to elect a new president.

Osmani is now running for parliament as a candidate for her former party, the Democratic League of Kosovo (LDK).

Speaking at an election campaign rally, she told supporters "You vote to decide whether Kosovo will be a state of its citizens or a state of only one man."

"Kurti and Osmani are politicians with opposing ideological orientations, who were united for the political synergy of the moment, being perceived by citizens as the hope of change, especially against corruption," political analyst and journalism professor Arben Fetoshi told DW.

Fetoshi went on to say that although the two differed on foreign policy and the subject of coordination with international partners, they did not have any major clashes during the four-year term of Kurti's government.

"Therefore, their rivalry in the current race mainly stems from the lack of support for Osmani's second mandate but does not exclude the personal dimension and ideological orientation of each," he said.

body.zh: 周日的科索沃选举是 16 个月内的第三次选举，前盟友总理阿尔宾·库尔蒂 (Albin Kurti) 与前总统维约萨·奥斯马尼 (Vjosa Osmani) 之间发生冲突，与塞尔维亚的对话陷入僵局，欧盟一体化面临障碍。 科索沃当前的竞选活动不仅表现为对立政党之间通常的竞争，而且还表现为该国近年来最重要的政治联盟之一的瓦解，即过去六年领导政府的总理阿尔宾·库尔蒂和前总统维约萨·奥斯马尼的联盟。 奥斯马尼已经是阿尔宾·库尔蒂的政治盟友，并在 2021 年被科索沃议会选举为总统时得到了总理的支持。 当时，两人被视为科索沃变革和反腐败斗争的动力。现在，他们是竞争对手。 今年早些时候，奥斯马尼的任期结束时，库尔蒂并不支持她连任。 库尔蒂曾表示，“总统应该是一个团结和具有代表性的人物”，在他看来，奥斯马尼有参与政党并寻求选民直接支持的政治野心。 相反，总理提出了来自他自己的政党 Vetevendosje 的候选人。但反对派议员并没有支持这些候选人。 周日举行的提前大选是科索沃不到 16 个月内的第三次大选，因科索沃议会 4 月份第二次未能选举新总统而引发。 奥斯马尼现在作为她的前政党科索沃民主联盟（LDK）的候选人竞选议会。 她在竞选集会上发表讲话时告诉支持者“你们投票决定科索沃是一个由其公民组成的国家还是一个只有一个人的国家。” 政治分析家兼新闻学教授阿尔本·费托什（Arben Fetoshi）告诉德国之声：“库尔蒂和奥斯马尼是意识形态取向相反的政治家，他们为了当前的政治协同效应而团结在一起，被公民视为变革的希望，特别是反对腐败的希望。” 费托希接着表示，尽管两人在外交政策以及与国际伙伴的协调问题上存在分歧，但在库尔蒂政府四年任期内没有发生任何重大冲突。 “因此，他们在当前竞选中的竞争主要源于奥斯马尼第二次任期缺乏支持，但并不排除每个人的个人维度和意识形态取向，”他说。 分析人士表示，对于一个仍在努力巩固民主制度、向欧盟靠拢并推进与邻国塞尔维亚对话的国家来说，科索沃看似无休无止的选举周期凸显了另一个重大问题，即其政治阶层无力建立制度......

When personal ambition or party loyalty overshadows the common good, progress can stall, hindering a nation's ability to address critical challenges and move forward.

title.en: 'Cockroach' movement gives voice to India's angry youth
title.zh: “蟑螂”运动为印度愤怒的青年发声

summary.en: The satirical Cockroach Janta Party has tapped into the concerns of the India's youth over issues plaguing the nation's education and employment policies.
summary.zh: 讽刺性的“蟑螂人民党”触及了印度青年对困扰国家教育和就业政策问题的担忧。

body.en:
The satirical Cockroach Janta Party has tapped into the concerns of the India's youth over issues plaguing the nation's education and employment policies.

The Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a movement that emerged from social media satire only weeks ago, is preparing to take its campaign onto India's streets.

Its founder Abhijeet Dipke, a 30-year-old Boston University graduate, said on Monday that he would return to India to lead a "peaceful protest" on June 6 demanding the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged exam irregularities.

"The time has come for all of us to come together, following the path of the Constitution of India, and peacefully raise our voices to demand Dharmendra Pradhan's resignation," Dipke said in a video posted on the CJP's Instagram handle on Monday. "If we raise our voices together, they will definitely have to listen to us," he added.

India's nationwide medical entrance test was canceled last month, but only after some 2.2 million students had already taken the exam. The authorities said the move was due to suspicions that exam questions had been leaked.

The CJP was set up after remarks attributed to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, who reportedly compared some unemployed young people to "cockroaches" and "parasites."

Kant later said his comments were taken out of context and that he was referring to those who use fake degrees.

But the remarks touched a raw nerve among many young Indians already struggling with unemployment, recurring examination scandals and growing economic insecurity.

Though Dipke launched the CJP as a satirical online project, it quickly took on a life of its own.

"There is this underlying feeling among [India's youth] that the current political system just does not care about them, be it the government party or the opposition," Dipke told The New York Times in a recent interview.

According to statements on the CJP website and social media platforms, the new group aims to create local chapters, recruit volunteers and campaign on issues ranging from joblessness and exam paper leaks to educational reform and government accountability.

Since its launch, the CJP   has established an immense social media following.

Its Instagram handle now has over 22 million followers — far more than the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party's (BJP) which has 9.5 million, and the main opposition Congress Party, with its 13.9 million.

Authorities have blocked the group's X account, however, citing national security concerns. This has prompted a legal challenge.

Some Indian leaders have alleged that the CJP is backed by India's enemies abroad.

Rajeev Chandrasekhar, a senior politician from Prime Minister Narendra Modi's  ...
body.zh: 具有讽刺意味的蟑螂简塔党利用了印度年轻人对困扰该国教育和就业政策问题的担忧。 蟑螂简塔党（CJP）是几周前从社交媒体讽刺中兴起的一个运动，现在正准备将其竞选活动带到印度街头。 其创始人、30 岁的波士顿大学毕业生阿比吉特·迪普克 (Abhijeet Dipke) 周一表示，他将于 6 月 6 日返回印度领导一场“和平抗议”，要求教育部长达门德拉·普拉丹 (Dharmendra Pradhan) 因涉嫌考试违规行为辞职。 周一，迪普克在 CJP Instagram 账号上发布的一段视频中表示，“现在是我们所有人团结起来，沿着印度宪法的道路，和平地发出我们的声音，要求达门德拉·普拉丹辞职的时候了。” “如果我们一起发出声音，他们肯定会听我们的，”他补充道。 印度全国医学入学考试上个月被取消，但此前已有约 220 万学生参加了考试。当局表示，此举是因为怀疑试题被泄露。 CJP 是在印度首席大法官苏里亚·康德 (Surya Kant) 发表言论后成立的，据报道，康德将一些失业年轻人比作“蟑螂”和“寄生虫”。 康德后来说，他的评论被断章取义，他指的是那些使用假学位的人。 但这些言论触动了许多已经在失业、考试丑闻和日益严重的经济不安全感中挣扎的印度年轻人的敏感神经。 尽管 Dipke 将 CJP 作为一个在线讽刺项目推出，但它很快就拥有了自己的生命力。 “[印度年轻人]有一种潜在的感觉，即当前的政治制度根本不关心他们，无论是政府党还是反对派，”迪普克在最近的一次采访中告诉《纽约时报》。 根据 CJP 网站和社交媒体平台上的声明，新组织的目标是创建地方分会、招募志愿者，并就失业和试卷泄露、教育改革和政府问责等问题开展活动。 自推出以来，CJP 已在社交媒体上建立了庞大的追随者。 它的 Instagram 帐号目前拥有超过 2200 万粉丝，远远超过执政党印度人民党 (BJP) 的 950 万粉丝和主要反对党国大党的 1390 万粉丝。 然而，当局以国家安全为由封锁了该组织的 X 账户。这引发了法律挑战。 一些印度领导人声称，印度共产党得到了印度海外敌人的支持。 拉吉夫·钱德拉塞卡 (Rajeev Chandrasekhar) 是纳伦德拉·莫迪总理领导下的高级政治家...

Proverbs 31:8 reminds us of the importance of speaking up for those who cannot speak for themselves. This story underscores the need for societies to listen to the frustrations of their...

title.en: Australia must engage with Solomon Islands with mutual respect. It’s about so much more than keeping Beijing at bay | Connor Graham

summary.en: The article discusses the recent change in government in the Solomon Islands, urging Australia to engage with the nation based on mutual respect rather than solely through the lens of regional competition with China.
summary.zh: 文章讨论了所罗门群岛最近的政府更迭，敦促澳大利亚以相互尊重为基础与该国接触，而不仅仅是从与中国进行区域竞争的角度来看待。

body.en: A change of government in Honiara is not just a development in regional competition with China When Matthew Wale won a parliamentary vote to become Solomon Islands’ prime minister last month, the questions came quickly. What does this mean for Beijing? Is this good news for Australia? This approach fosters genuine relationships built on dignity rather...

title.en: Taiwan's Lai: Status quo is key to secure tech supply chains
title.zh: 台湾赖清德：维持现状是确保科技供应链的关键

summary.en: Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te stated at an AI and tech summit in Taipei that maintaining the status quo is crucial for securing global tech supply chains. Taiwan is a key chipmaker, and its relationship with China presents ongoing risks to this vital industry.
summary.zh: 台湾总统赖清德在台北举行的AI与科技峰会上表示，维持现状对于确保科技供应链安全至关重要。台湾是全球关键的芯片制造商，而其与中国的关系持续带来风险。

body.zh: 赖清德总统在台北召开人工智能和技术峰会，表示维持现状是确保供应链安全的关键。台湾是重要的芯片制造商，但其与中国大陆的关系始终是风险来源。 台湾总统赖清德周二在台北举行的电脑展开幕式上表示，维持政治现状是台湾为确保全球供应链安全可以采取的最负责任的做法。 作为全球最大的代工芯片制造商台积电 (TSMC) 的所在地，台湾是英伟达 (Nvidia) 和苹果 (Apple) 等公司的主要设备供应商。 但鉴于中国声称该岛应是其领土的一部分，其政治地位一直是摩擦的根源。几十年来，一种令人不安的僵局一直持续着，北京既不放弃对台湾的主权主张，也不允许其他国家在外交上承认这个岛国，但也不对其试图夺取台湾领土的威胁采取行动。 黎智英在台北世界贸易中心告诉来自各科技巨头的高管，他的政府和领土对他们的行业越来越重要。 赖说：“随着世界对人工智能的需求不断增长，也越来越需要一个稳定、值得信赖、有能力承担责任的台湾。” 他说：“政府将坚定维护台湾海峡的和平与稳定，并致力于维持现状。”他指的是分隔台湾和中国大陆的狭长海域。 大型语言模型和机器学习工具（通常被称为“人工智能”）依赖于高端芯片和半导体制造商。 Nvidia 首席执行官黄仁勋是开幕当天的其他发言者之一，一周前，这家市值极高的芯片公司宣布计划每年在台湾投资约 1500 亿美元（约合 1290 亿欧元）。 “台湾在制造业方面令人难以置信，尤其是技术制造。这是生态系统的中心，”黄说。 在美国总统唐纳德·特朗普最近访问中国与他的对手习近平会谈期间，台湾的地位是一个备受关注的话题。 在那次访问期间，特朗普表示美国将暂停对台北的新一轮军事援助，这也因在采访中抱怨台湾如何从美国“窃取”芯片产业而引起关注。 与德国和世界上大多数国家一样，美国在台湾问题上也小心谨慎。一方面，它坚持北京要求的“一个中国”政策，只是正式承认一个中国国家。另一方面，它也是台湾最重要的靠山和安全保证者，也是主要的贸易...

reflection.en: President Lai's emphasis on preserving the status quo for secure tech supply chains reflects a prudent approach to navigating complex geopolitical risks. In a world of constant change and potential disruption, wisdom calls us to foresee dangers and take thoughtful steps to protect vital interests and foster stability. This foresight helps communities and...
reflection.zh: 赖清德总统强调维持现状以确保科技供应链安全，这反映了在复杂地缘政治风险中采取审慎的态度。在一个充满变数和潜在干扰的世界里，智慧呼吁我们预见危险，并采取深思熟虑的步骤来保护重要利益，促进稳定。这种远见有助于社群和国家建立抵御未来挑战的韧性。

title.en: China goes after 'ghost kitchens' to rein in cut-throat food delivery apps
title.zh: 中国打击“幽灵厨房”以遏制竞争激烈的食品配送应用

summary.en: Chinese authorities are targeting thousands of "ghost kitchens," which are online food shops that lack a physical presence, causing concern among consumers.
summary.zh: 中国当局正在打击数千家“幽灵厨房”，这些线上餐饮店没有实际的实体店面，引发了消费者的担忧。

body.en:
Chinese authorities have taken aim at a new target as they rein in the country's cut-throat food delivery industry: "ghost kitchens", or restaurants that don't actually exist but appear on apps.

The "ghost kitchens" outsource orders to third-party vendors, which fulfill them at lower costs, allowing merchants to push down prices and maximise profits.

Authorities have found thousands of these "ghost kitchens" across China, raising concerns that the cheap prices are coming at the cost of food safety.

Starting this week, apps must verify restaurants' licences and addresses, while merchants must ensure the listing online matches the physical business and specify if it offers dine-in services.

The scrutiny of "ghost kitchens" began last year, after a man in Beijing lodged a complaint over an unsatisfactory cake topped with inedible flowers. He had ordered it on a food delivery app, state media reported.

Officials found that the cake chain he had ordered from listed nearly 380 locations on major e-commerce platforms but did not have a single physical store. Its online shops also allegedly used forged business licences.

As the investigation continued, it revealed that the chain accepted orders which were then transferred to a different platform - and that is where the orders were outsourced to various third-party vendors, depending on who had the lowest bid.

Authorities found a total of 3.6 million cake orders across two order-transfer platforms, state news agency Xinhua reported last month.

They also recorded 67,000 "ghost shops" across seven major food delivery apps, which together with the order-transfer sites "formed an illegal supply chain through mutual collusion", according to Xinhua.

Food delivery platforms were complicit in these arrangements, it added. "If we're too strict in our review, the merchants would go to other platforms," a staff member from one delivery app reportedly told officials.

Last year, a price war among major delivery apps led to government warnings about a race to the bottom. Bearing the brunt of ever-speedier takeouts are delivery riders scrambling to meet tight deadlines for a pittance.

In April, the State Administration for Market Regulation said that they have fined seven e-commerce platforms - including Taobao, JD.com, Meituan and Pinduoduo - a total of 3.6bn yuan ($530m; £400m), mostly over deliveries from "ghost kitchens".

As the campaign against "ghost kitchens" continues, merchants are trying to assure consumers of food safety.

According to a Xinhua report, more than 20 takeout stalls in the eastern city of Hangzhou have installed "transparent kitchens" with live broadcasting features, allowing consumers to view food preparation in real time.

body.zh: 中国当局在控制该国竞争激烈的食品配送行业时瞄准了一个新目标：“幽灵厨房”，即实际上并不存在但出现在应用程序上的餐馆。 “幽灵厨房”将订单外包给第三方供应商，第三方供应商以更低的成本完成订单，从而使商家能够压低价格，实现利润最大化。 当局在中国各地发现了数千个这样的“鬼厨房”，引发了人们的担忧，人们担心低价是以牺牲食品安全为代价的。 从本周开始，应用程序必须验证餐馆的执照和地址，而商家必须确保在线列表与实体店相符，并注明是否提供堂食服务。 去年，北京一名男子对一款不令人满意的蛋糕进行投诉，蛋糕上铺满了不可食用的鲜花，随后，对“幽灵厨房”的审查就开始了。据官方媒体报道，他是在一款食品配送应用程序上订购的。 执法人员发现，他所订购的蛋糕连锁店在各大电商平台上有近380家门店，但没有一家实体店。据称，其网上商店还使用伪造的营业执照。 随着调查的继续，它发现该连锁店接受了订单，然后将其转移到另一个平台 - 订单被外包给各个第三方供应商，具体取决于谁的出价最低。 据官方通讯社新华社上个月报道，当局在两个订单转移平台上发现了总计 360 万份蛋糕订单。 据新华社报道，他们还记录了七大外卖应用程序中的 6.7 万家“鬼店”，它们与订单转移网站“相互勾结，形成了非法供应链”。 它补充说，食品配送平台是这些安排的同谋。据报道，一款配送应用程序的一名工作人员告诉官员：“如果我们审查过于严格，商家就会转向其他平台。” 去年，主要配送应用程序之间的价格战导致政府对竞价行为发出警告。外卖速度越来越快，首当其冲的是那些为了微薄的利润而争先恐后地在紧迫的时间内完成任务的送货骑手。 今年 4 月，国家市场监管总局表示，他们对淘宝、京东、美团和拼多多等 7 个电子商务平台处以总计 36 亿元人民币（5.3 亿美元；4 亿英镑）的罚款，大部分罚款都来自“幽灵厨房”的配送。 随着打击“鬼厨房”行动的持续进行，商家正在努力向消费者保证食品安全。 据新华社报道，东部城市杭州的20多家外卖摊位安装了具有直播功能的“透明厨房”，让消费者可以实时查看食物的制作过程。 在附近的安徽省，当局上周宣布……

reflection.en: The rise of "ghost kitchens" highlights the tension between fierce competition and ethical business practices. When businesses operate without transparency, consumer trust erodes, reminding us of the importance of honesty in all dealings.
reflection.zh: “幽灵厨房”的兴起凸显了激烈竞争与商业道德之间的张力。当企业缺乏透明度时，消费者的信任就会受到侵蚀，这提醒我们所有交易中诚实的重要性。

title.en: Watch: Glass doors break as fans scramble to see Pursuit of Jade star

summary.en: Huge crowds formed outside a shopping centre in China to see actor Zhang Linghe.
summary.zh: 大批人群聚集在中国一家购物中心外，只为一睹演员张凌赫的风采。

body.en:
Footage from social media shows the moment glass doors outside a shopping centre in Nanning, southern China, shattered as fans waited to see actor Zhang Linghe on Sunday.

The 28-year-old, who stars in Chinese historial drama Pursuit of Jade, was due to appear at a Molsion eyewear event.

Other videos from social media show packed crowds gathered around balconies within the mall. Organisers later cancelled the in-person event and moved it online.

In a statement on Sunday night, Linghe's studio said: "The brand event originally scheduled for today has been temporarily rescheduled, and we sincerely apologize for any inconvenience caused.

It added that the actor and his studio would reimburse travel and accommodation costs for fans who travelled from afar to attend the event.

Molsion said medical check-ups had been arranged for fans who "sustained minor injuries", it added it would upgrade safety measures to ensure "smooth and safe" future events.

title.en: Taiwan opposition leader heads to US

body.en:
KMT leader Cheng Li-wun is traveling to the US for a two-week visit. She has indicated she is "very interested" in meeting President Donald Trump but could face a grilling over her stance on China relations.

The leader of Taiwan's main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), Cheng Li-wun, on Monday heads to the United States for a two-week visit.

The trip comes two months after her visit to China , where she met with President Xi Jinping and spoke of there being a need for work to "promote reconciliation across the Strait and create regional prosperity and peace."

China views Taiwan, which is governed independently, as a breakaway province and has not ruled out the use of force in taking it back.

With the US being Taiwan's primary military supporter, Cheng is likely to be questioned on her role in blocking a Taiwanese government plan to spend nearly $40 billion (€34 billion) on weapons , including US arms.

On the question of her willingness to meet with US President Donald Trump, Cheng told a press conference: "I am of course very willing."

She said she was prepared to meet with anyone who is "conducive to peace" and who has a strong position of authority, much like her meeting with China's leader.

"The same applies to President Trump. Anything that is helpful to peace, I am willing to do; anyone who is helpful to peace, I am willing to meet — let alone the most critical decision-maker and leader, which is the president of the United States," Cheng was quoted as saying by the Reuters news agency.

Cheng is expected to visit San Francisco, Boston, New York, Washington and Los Angeles.

According to her trip itinerary, there are plans for her to meet with US lawmakers, government officials, as well as various think tanks and supporters.

Ahead of her visit, Cheng said she was hopeful her party can play a key role in regional peace efforts and "gain deeper trust from the US."

title.en: How China keeps North Korea's economy alive

body.en:
Pyongyang relies on China for 95% of its legitimate trade; hacking, arms deals and remittances also help it stay afloat.

North Korea runs one of the most bizarre economies on the planet. Despite being one of only a handful of nations with nuclear weapons , its 2024 gross domestic product (GDP) was a paltry $26.6 billion (€22.9 billion).

This is about 70 times smaller than South Korea's $1.86 trillion economy and about a fifth of the annual revenue of the world's top-traded company, Nvidia.

Thanks to a centrally planned economy that prioritizes domestic production, North Korea is nowhere near as reliant on trade as your average free-market economy, partly due to international sanctions, introduced by the United Nations in 2017 over its nuclear weapons and ballistic missiles program.

The North's total imports and exports account for just a small fraction of GDP, versus the South, where international trade makes up around 80% of the economy, according to the World Bank.

You could say that China plays almost an exclusive role in North Korea's minimal reliance on trade .

According to the Washington-based think tank the National Committee on North Korea , Pyongyang depends on China for up to 95% of total trade and 85% of its exports.

Almost all imports also come from China. In 2024, North Korea's legitimate imports totaled just $2.33 billion — tiny by global standards.

With no domestic oil production, these deliveries from China include petroleum and other fuels and are essential in keeping the economy functioning, along with food, textiles, machinery, electronics and vehicles.

This gives Beijing enormous economic clout over North Korean leader Kim Jong Un . A recent report suggested that US President Donald Trump is now trying to leverage that muscle to bring Pyongyang back to the negotiating table over its contentious nuclear weapons program.

South Korea's Yonhap news agency reported recently that Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to visit Pyongyang in the next few weeks, playing a key mediator role to help bridge the gap between Trump and Kim in the long-running dispute. Beijing is yet to confirm the trip.

Legitimate exports from what the US labels a rogue state are even less impressive. According to the Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency, North Korea's exports barely reached $360 million in 2024.

Those foreign sales are strikingly modest, with fake hair and wigs the country's only best seller, making up about 40% of exports, primarily to China, which then reexports them to the rest of the world.

body.en: Twin threats from east and west have clearly made the bloc more appealing – but its rule-bound institutions need urgent attention Giant butter mountains, wine lakes and an apocryphal EU ban on bendy bananas formed the mythological backdrop to Britain’s 2016 Brexit referendum debacle. Yet while many Vote Leave claims were exaggerated, inaccurate or blatantly untrue, the EU’s capacity for laying itself open to ridicule is undiminished 10 years on. Take the strange case of the whingeing EU commissioners, annoyed that their officially provided electric vehicles cannot manage the time-consuming 280-mile journey between Brussels and Strasbourg without stopping to recharge. This important issue, first reported by Politico , raises vital questions. Do these highly paid bureaucrats really need chauffeur-driven “company cars”? Surely they could catch a train, or fly, or cycle. EV use is mandatory for road trips. The vehicles are supplied in line with the EU’s Green Deal emissions-cutting policy, which commissioners might be expected to support, not carp about. body.en:
The news that Australia will only receive "second-hand" Virginia-class submarines has become the latest fault line in the AUKUS debate, with critics questioning ballooning costs and questioning the value for money.

"You've paid for a Porsche, but they give you a compact two-seater," Albert Palazzo, adjunct professor at UNSW in Canberra and a former director of war studies for the Australian Army, told SBS News.

"If I was the consumer, I'd get angry. I paid for a Porsche, where's my Porsche?"

Under the agreement made in 2023 with the United States and United Kingdom , Australia would buy three Virginia-class nuclear-powered submarines from the US — one newly built, and two already 'in service'.

Last week, Defence Minister Richard Marles revealed that all three of the submarines would be in-service vessels from the US Navy. Marles said the new approach would be "cost-effective" and "streamline" the submarines' delivery.

Speaking to ABC radio on Wednesday, Defence Industry Minister Pat Conroy said the arrangement was always the government's wish, and that it would be "simpler, cheaper to manage, and that's been confirmed by the Pentagon overnight as well".

A Virginia-class submarine is expected to have three refurbishments in its 33-year lifespan.

Jennifer Parker, a maritime security expert at the Australian National University Security College, said it's possible unforeseen costs could arise depending on the condition of the submarines.

It's unclear whether the US would refurbish the submarines before giving them to Australia, but Parker said it's reasonable to assume they would.

"If it is already of the age that it needs to have gone through its first one, which is about the 10-year mark, then you would expect that we would get [a refit]," she told SBS News.

Parker said it's a reassuring sign that Australia was receiving Virginia-class submarines, as opposed to the older Los Angeles-class submarines reaching the end of their life.

"I was a little bit surprised because I thought they might sell off the Los Angeles-class because they have less need for those," she said.

The 'in service' Virginia-class submarines Australia will receive are Block IV boats. They're 125m long and fitted with 12 missile launchers.

Later models of the Virginia-class submarine expanded their capability, with Block V growing to 140m in length and carrying 40 missiles.

body.en:
The defence minister is being urged by the Opposition to haul backbencher Ed Husic into line after the Labor MP broke ranks to call for a rethink of the AUKUS nuclear submarine deal.

Husic went public with his reservations about the pact following revelations Australia will only get second-hand submarines from the United States under the agreement.

His comments follow Midnight Oil frontman and former Labor minister Peter Garrett announcing plans for an independent "people's inquiry" into the national security implications of AUKUS.

Husic, who also questioned the deal during a private caucus meeting on Tuesday, said Australia needed to reconsider its commitment to the deal with the US and the United Kingdom because the US was becoming an increasingly unreliable ally.

"You do wonder whether or not we will get the deal, even the reconfigured one that we have got," the western Sydney MP told reporters at Parliament House.

Australia was set to get a mix of new and used Virginia-Class vessels before eventually building its own in Adelaide, but now the defence force will only get used submarines.

Defence Minister Richard Marles defended the move, saying it would make AUKUS simpler and cheaper to deliver, but Husic appeared sceptical.

The Labor MP, who was science and industry minister before being ousted from cabinet in 2025 in a factional power play, said Australia needed to be open about the workforce shortages, supply chain challenges and quality issues confronting the AUKUS pact.

Husic has previously broken with his colleagues on the recognition of a Palestinian state, the war in Gaza and taxation of gas.

Opposition defence spokesperson James Paterson said the defence minister needed to pull Husic into line and suggested the comments could undermine Australia's relationship with the US and UK.

"It's absolutely legitimate to ask questions about how this government is going about delivering AUKUS ... the answer to those concerns is to double down," he told reporters in Canberra.

On Tuesday, Garrett announced plans to lead a community-based inquiry into AUKUS, investigating the implications of the pact for the nation's security.

The crowdfunded probe, run separately from the government, would look into whether the vessels would make Australia more secure, the storage of nuclear waste and potential long-term strategic consequences, the former environment minister said.

"This is not a royal commission, this is a people's inquiry," Garrett said in Canberra.

summary.en: Behind one school's blue-tongued lizard lies a deeper story about kinship and Country.

body.en:
It's National Reconciliation Week and this year's theme — 'All In' — is a call for all Australians to take meaningful action towards reconciliation every day.

At St Bernadette's Primary School in western Sydney on Dharug Country, that commitment is taking shape through a unique classroom project centred on one of Australia's best-known native reptiles — the blue-tongued lizard.

As part of its cultural learning program, the school has adopted the lizard as its totem, using it to teach students about Aboriginal culture, caring for Country and the importance of protecting local wildlife.

Year 4 students Penny and Lillian are among those helping to build a new garden habitat for the totem — affectionately known on campus as 'Bluey' — planting vegetation and creating what Lillian describes as "a safe place for it to stay" near the school office.

For many Aboriginal communities, totems are more than symbols: they reflect spiritual, cultural, and environmental ties between people, animals and the land. At St Bernadette's Primary, that understanding is being brought to life through a familiar visitor to the school grounds as a lesson in culture, responsibility and belonging.

The school's principal, Lisa Samojlowicz, says the idea emerged during conversations with an Indigenous parent about ways to incorporate First Nations education into the school curriculum.

"When talking with one of my parents, who is an Indigenous man, we were talking about our National Reconciliation celebrations and the different activities he might support us in developing and we started talking about the totem," she tells SBS News

"We've had the blue-tongued lizard in and out of our gardens since before. And we notice them on the gardens, on the pathway, sunning themselves."

What began as a small reconciliation activity has since evolved into a broader school-wide project.

The garden project has grown in popularity with support from the Jarara Cultural Centre's Junior Rangers program, including former students like Thomas Ross.

"When we do initiatives like this, tapping into our local knowledge, we allow for our kids to become deeper into our environment and feel like they belong in this place," he tells SBS News.

Educators say the project is also creating opportunities for students to learn about the deeper cultural meaning behind totems and kinship systems in Aboriginal communities.

For staff involved in the project, understanding what a totem means — and how these meanings vary across communities — is just as important as the reptile itself.

body.en:
Dementia is now Australia's biggest killer. Insight examines how patients, carers and the government's support systems are equipping themselves to manage this public health crisis. Watch Insight episode Dealing With Dementia on SBS On Demand.

With two generations of women in my family touched by dementia, the question I ask myself is: will I be next?

I recently did some DNA testing for my overall health and ticked a box to say I didn't want to know about the genes for Alzheimer's.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

And though there was a part of me that 'knew' what was coming, I was still shocked.

Everyone has two apolipoprotein E (ApoE) genes, which are a type of gene linked to a predisposition to Alzheimer's.

While I found out I have an ApoE2, which carries a decreased risk of developing the disease, I also found out I have an ApoE4 gene. This latter gene increases my risk of developing the disease, but it does not make it certain.

But to me, it feels like a loaded gun, and I don't know if or when it will go off.

When my mother Moira, 76, was first diagnosed with Alzheimer's, we did everything to preserve her life.

With a front-row seat to her own mother's suffering with the disease until age 102, Mum was petrified of developing it also.

Mum became acutely anxious when she received the diagnosis and made it very clear she wanted to end her life before she couldn't recognise her family.

She knew there was nothing on offer in Australia for those with dementia to access Voluntary Assisted Dying (VAD), and that she would need to do it herself.

We've had conversations over the years about how she'd prefer to end her life — some of which I filmed for a documentary.

He cared for her at home for 10 years before she had to enter a locked memory support unit in residential aged care during COVID, where she still lives today.

I feel so sad when I visit Mum. These wards are full of devastatingly sad, confused and desperate faces staring back at you.

It's a kind of parallel hellhole universe, which is, of course, no reflection on the people and organisations behind these facilities, who are doing an amazing service.

Mum is now nonverbal, so it is difficult to know if she's in pain or has any joy.

She was a very lovable, selfless powerhouse of a mum. To see her autonomy and life sucked away — her curiosity, capacity to communicate, empathy, cheekiness, love of reading, travel and art — feels barbaric.

What remains is a sentient soul who craves cuddles, listens to music, has a good appetite and is able-bodied.

summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及智慧、知识与追求真理。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Australia's national science agency has defended its ability to deliver research and technology, as it confirmed significant job losses.

In November, the Commonwealth Scientific and Industrial Research Organisation (CSIRO) said up to 350 research positions would be slashed as the "cost of doing science has gone up".

Originally, almost half of those jobs were expected to come from the agency's environmental research unit, which includes climate adaptation science.

But executives from the agency confirmed during budget estimates on Tuesday evening that while 92 staff from the unit are affected, 86 roles will be made redundant.

CSIRO acting chief executive Elanor Huntington said there had been a change in the "composition" of the job cuts.

"We've received a very significant amount of feedback through that process, all of which we've read and thought about very carefully," she told the public hearing.

"We have a six-stage major change process. We have now reached step five ... we have confirmed with all of the affected research units the final sets of changes."

Huntington said the organisation would need to source an additional $135 million each year over the next decade to remain financially sustainable.

The cuts attracted widespread criticism, including from senior climate scientists and experts internationally, who claimed the CSIRO's science capability would be severely impacted.

Peter Mayfield, CSIRO's executive director for environment, said management had been "very careful" with where reductions were made.

He said the agency remained confident it could meet the obligations for a key project providing projections on climate change.

"We're not walking away from anything. We're actively trying to make sure we do well around climate science," Mayfield said.

The federal budget handed down in May set aside more than $387 million for the CSIRO over the next four years.

The Community and Public Sector Union warned the extra funding was not enough to stop the science agency from shedding staff.

Since February 2024, 1,150 jobs have been cut from the CSIRO, union secretary Susan Tonks previously said.

title.en: Government waives gag orders for defence sexual violence survivors ahead of inquiry
title.zh: 政府在调查前放弃为性暴力幸存者辩护的禁言令

summary.en: Recommended by the Royal Commission into Defence and Veteran Suicide, the inquiry is due to begin later in 2026.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Survivors of sexual violence in the Australian military will be able to discuss their abuse at an upcoming inquiry after the government waived gag orders preventing them giving evidence.

Veterans Affairs' Minister Matt Keogh has written to victims saying the government will not seek to enforce any non-disclosure agreements (NDAs).

The move comes after a campaign by those who had suffered abuse, whistleblowers and civil society organisations.

"Veterans who served this country should not have to ask permission to speak about their lived experiences of military sexual violence," Julia Delaforce, a former RAAF airwoman and whistleblower, said.

"This amnesty is a critical step towards lifting the legal gag on military sexual violence survivors, so they can safely speak to the upcoming inquiry and help expose the institutional systems that failed them."
